title: Wudu guide for a new Muslim
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 11 (Pupil PDF worksheet: wudu guide for a new Muslim)
intro: Lesson 11: Wudu: fard, sunnah and what breaks it. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Qur'an, al-Ma'idah 5:6 (translation of the meaning)
paras: O you who believe, when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows, wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles.

blocks.title: Sort into: Fard / Sunnah
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Fard, Sunnah.
blocks.answer: Fard: Washing the face; Washing arms to the elbows; Wiping the head; Washing feet to the ankles. Sunnah: Using the siwak; Washing three times; Starting with the right; Rinsing between the fingers

panels.title: Order and continuity
points: Rinsing mouth and nose: obligatory for Hanbalis

panels.title: What breaks wudu?
points: Anything from the two private passages
Differed on: eating camel meat, touching the private part

blocks.h: Wudu guide for a new Muslim

keywords.def: obligatory: leaving it makes the act invalid
recommended: following the Prophet ﷺ, rewarded but not obligatory

questions.q: Explain why washing three times is sunnah, not fard.
questions.a: The ayah commands washing, which is done once; the Prophet ﷺ sometimes washed once, twice or three times, so three is sunnah.

questions.q: Name two sunnah acts of wudu.
questions.a: For example: siwak, three times, starting with the right

questions.q: Make a 'wudu guide for a new Muslim' on the pupil PDF: the steps in order, with F (fard) or S (sunnah) beside each, and a box of three things that break wudu.
questions.a: Correct order; fard: face, arms, head, feet (with order and continuity per many scholars); sunnah labelled; breakers correct

questions.q: Extend: what should someone do if unsure whether wudu broke?
questions.a: Stay with certainty: wudu remains (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: Stretch: why might scholars differ on camel meat?
questions.a: They understood the evidence differently: some took the command as obligatory, others as recommended or abrogated.

questions.q: Hamza forgets to wipe his head. His wudu is ...
options: Invalid: wiping the head is fard
Valid if he washed his face
questions.a: A) Invalid: wiping the head is fard. Wiping the head is named in 5:6, so it is fard.

questions.q: Washing the face in wudu is ...
Think again: is wudu valid if you miss a sunnah? A fard?
questions.a: Sunnah missed: valid. Fard missed: not valid.
